ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: If a mutation occurs in which uracil is deleted from the messenger RNA after methionine is translated, what is the resulting amino acid sequence?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If a mutation occurs in which uracil is deleted from the messenger RNA after methionine is translated, what is the resulting amino acid sequence?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the image shows the original mRNA sequence as AUG CCA CUA GCA CGU, and the corresponding translation as Methionine, Proline, Leucine, Alanine, Arginine. The lower part of the image is an mRNA codon table, from which it can be found that CCA corresponds to proline, CAG corresponds to glutamine, and CAC corresponds to histidine. Reasoning: The question states that after methionine has already been translated, one uracil U in the mRNA is deleted, so the first codon AUG still translates as Methionine. Delete the U in the subsequent sequence, namely the U in CUA, and the remaining bases are regrouped by triplets as CCA, CAG, CAC, with the incomplete base at the end ignored. According to the codon table, CCA = proline, CAG = glutamine, CAC = histidine. Therefore, the resulting sequence is Methionine-proline-glutamine-histidine.
